subject: Pyramid of Khufu
claim: The completed Great Pyramid stood about 146.5 metres high and was entirely cased in high-quality Tura limestone.
value_text: 146.5 m high with Tura limestone casing
uncertainty: Literal mirror reflectivity and perfectly flawless edges are illustrative rather than asserted by the source.

subject: Pyramid of Khufu
claim: A modern reconstruction of the four original casing baselines gives a mean side of approximately 230.363 metres.
value_text: approximately 230.363 m
uncertainty: No original corner survives and the reconstructed baselines extrapolate from partial surviving evidence.

subject: Pyramid of Khafre
claim: Khafre's pyramid originally stood about 143.5 metres high and was cased in polished high-quality Tura limestone.
value_text: 143.5 m high with polished Tura limestone casing
uncertainty: Exact construction and completion dates vary among modern chronologies.

subject: Pyramid of Khafre
claim: The survey-derived guide represents Khafre's base at approximately 215.3 metres square.
value_text: approximately 215.3 m
locator: Giza Pyramids Corners and Centers dataset
uncertainty: Rounded from a copyrighted illustration dataset derived largely from Petrie; do not treat as a redistributed survey product.

subject: Pyramid of Menkaure
claim: Menkaure's pyramid stood about 65 metres high; its lower quarter used granite and the remainder limestone, and much of the granite was left unsmoothed when the king died.
value_text: 65 m high; granite lower quarter; limestone above; incomplete finish
uncertainty: This directly conflicts with the requested wholly white and perfectly finished casing.

subject: Pyramid of Menkaure
claim: The survey-derived guide represents Menkaure's base at approximately 105.55 metres square.
value_text: approximately 105.55 m
locator: Giza Pyramids Corners and Centers dataset
uncertainty: Rounded guide value; the historic monument has unequal sides and complex casing conditions.

subject: Royal pyramid complexes
claim: A royal pyramid complex joined the pyramid and adjacent pyramid temple to a more distant valley temple by a causeway, with subsidiary or queens' pyramids in some complexes.
value_text: pyramid temple causeway valley temple and subsidiary pyramids
uncertainty: Individual complex plans and preservation differ; this does not fix exact local coordinates.

subject: Pyramid causeways
claim: Old Kingdom pyramid causeways could be roofed or enclosed and decorated, but exact surviving evidence differs by complex.
value_text: covered or enclosed causeways
locator: Digital Giza FAQ discussion of causeways
uncertainty: The request treats all three as long straight covered corridors; exact roof form and completion are interpretive.

subject: Giza subsidiary pyramids
claim: The visual guide uses the documented grouping of three queens' pyramids and one satellite for Khufu, one satellite for Khafre, and three queens' pyramids for Menkaure.
value_text: Khufu 4; Khafre 1; Menkaure 3
uncertainty: Exact dimensions and completion states of individual small pyramids are simplified in the guide.

subject: Giza plateau
claim: The three principal complexes descend southwestward from Khufu to Khafre to Menkaure, while their causeways run generally eastward toward valley complexes.
value_text: published plateau-plan relationships
uncertainty: Local project coordinates are an approximate visual translation, not a georeferenced digitization.

subject: Three main Giza pyramids
claim: The survey dataset gives Khufu centre E 499999.990, N 100000.018, elevation 60.400 m; Khafre E 499666.012, N 99645.607, elevation 70.500 m; and Menkaure E 499426.477, N 99259.866, elevation 73.100 m. Transformed to project-local coordinates with Khufu at [0.000, 300.000, 0.000], the centres are Khafre [-333.978, -54.411, 10.100] and Menkaure [-573.513, -440.152, 12.700].
locator: Giza Pyramids Corners and Centers dataset
uncertainty: The millimetre-formatted values preserve the dataset's stated numerical precision but do not imply millimetre archaeological certainty. The project subtracts the Khufu survey centre and elevation, then adds 300 metres to local Y; the copyrighted dataset is cited but not redistributed.

subject: Great Sphinx
claim: The Great Sphinx combines a human royal head wearing the nemes headdress with a recumbent lion body, measures approximately 73.5 metres long, 19 metres wide, and 20 metres high, and is generally attributed to Khafre's reign.
value_text: human head on lion body; 73.5 x 19 x 20 m
uncertainty: Khafre attribution is strong but not absolute. The overall measurements support a semantic guide envelope, not exact reconstructed anatomy, facial appearance, component ratios, or clearance at a chosen year.

subject: Great Sphinx
claim: The Sphinx and its temple lie beside Khafre's valley temple and the lower part of his causeway.
value_text: beside Khafre valley temple and lower causeway
uncertainty: The preview envelope is schematic and does not encode a stone-by-stone survey.

subject: Great Sphinx
claim: AERA's mapped north elevation states that the Great Sphinx faces east.
value_text: east-facing long axis
uncertainty: Due-east orientation is evidence-backed; the project's point centre and simplified component proportions remain implementation guides rather than a survey mesh.

subject: Sphinx complex
claim: The Sphinx stands in a quarried ditch whose south side forms the north side of Khafre's causeway foundation, while the Sphinx Temple and Khafre Valley Temple share the prepared terrace in front of it.
value_text: Sphinx ditch north of causeway; temples on eastern terrace
locator: Sphinx quarry and temple terrace sections
uncertainty: The broad adjacency and separation are supported, but the local polygon, ditch depth, wall profile, construction debris, and exact clearance at approximately 2500 BCE remain needs-review implementation choices.

subject: Giza lower complexes
claim: Remote-sensing and topographic analysis reconstruct a lagoon-like Giza Inlet connected to the Ahramat Branch; the Khafre, Menkaure, and Khentkawes causeways lead to the inlet, while Khufu appears to connect more directly to the branch.
value_text: lagoon-like Giza Inlet adjoining lower complexes
locator: Results, "The western tributaries of the Ahramat Branch"; Figure 7 and caption
uncertainty: The inlet footprint and contemporaneity are remotely reconstructed; Figure 7 does not establish an exact 2500 BCE shoreline, depth, season, or uniform docking arrangement for all complexes.

subject: Khentkawes basin
claim: Excavation east of Khentkawes Town exposed a quarried basin whose banks were reinforced with crushed limestone debris and mudbrick, with stepped terraces and right-angle corners at the north end.
value_text: excavated constructed basin with reinforced banks
locator: Annual Report 2013–2014, pp. 12–13, "Giza's Back Bay: Marina Del Rey"
uncertainty: The excavated northern basin lies at Khentkawes Town, not at each pyramid valley temple; its original full extent and first-use date are not completely exposed.

subject: Khentkawes basin
claim: Basin silts, aquatic snail shells associated with deep quiet water, and the built basin form support standing Nile water and flood-season boat access at the lower plateau.
value_text: standing-water basin connected to flood-season waterways
locator: Annual Report 2013–2014, pp. 12–13, "Signs of Standing Water"
uncertainty: Aquatic remains support standing water but do not fix the water level at 2500 BCE; boat access and Nile connection are functional interpretations, not direct observation of an intact channel.

subject: Menkaure Valley Temple
claim: AERA investigators reconstruct the excavated basin as part of a channel extending toward Menkaure's Valley Temple, providing a plausible flood-season harbor connection.
value_text: inferred channel from excavated basin toward Menkaure Valley Temple
locator: Annual Report 2013–2014, p. 12, "Evidence of Ancient Harbor"
uncertainty: The report explicitly presents the connecting channel and harbor configuration as a possible reconstruction; the intervening route is not fully excavated and much of it lies beneath a modern cemetery.

subject: Giza eastern plateau foot
property: Khufu branch level and harbor access
claim: Pollen-derived reconstruction indicates that the Khufu branch remained at a relatively high level during the reigns of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure and enabled navigation to the pyramid harbor complex.
value_text: navigable Khufu branch and seasonally supplied harbor system
locator: Abstract; Figure 1; Figure 2 and discussion of Khufu-branch levels
uncertainty: The pollen proxy constrains relative branch level, not an exact 2500 BCE shoreline, inlet width, water depth, or season; larger cargo vessels were probably most viable during the annual flood.

subject: Three great pyramids
claim: The requested image presents all three main pyramids in smooth polished white limestone with pristine sharp edges.
value_text: all-white pristine casing
uncertainty: Cinematic alternative: conflicts with Menkaure's granite lower casing and unfinished surface.

subject: Giza plateau
claim: The requested image removes rubble and ruins, clears the Sphinx enclosure, and presents a clean completion state in warm low sunlight.
value_text: clean idealized completion state
uncertainty: Sand clearance, debris removal, precise weather, and simultaneous newness are illustrative.

subject: Giza reconstruction
claim: The later brief prioritizes verified history over the earlier all-white simultaneous-completion alternative and permits sober likely completion where evidence is incomplete.
value_text: evidence-led historical pass
uncertainty: This governs presentation choices but is not archaeological evidence.

subject: Khafre Valley Temple
claim: Khafre's valley temple used massive limestone blocks encased in granite, alabaster floors, and monolithic granite pillars.
value_text: massive limestone with granite casing and alabaster floors
uncertainty: A distant panorama can show the red granite massing and pale pavement but should not invent a fully visible interior plan.

subject: Pyramid of Khafre
claim: Excavated evidence supports a narrow basal band of reddish granite beneath Khafre's predominantly Tura-limestone casing.
value_text: one or possibly two basal granite courses
uncertainty: The exact visible number of courses around the whole pyramid is not uniform or completely preserved.

subject: Khufu pyramid temple
claim: Khufu's pyramid temple had a black basalt pavement and courtyard walls with carved and painted limestone reliefs; adjacent royal boat pits were stone-covered.
value_text: black basalt court with relief walls and sealed boat pits
uncertainty: The complete wall elevations and relief program are reconstructed from fragmentary remains; keep relief color subtle at this scale.

subject: Menkaure pyramid complex
claim: After Menkaure's death, Shepseskaf completed the valley temple in mudbrick; the official monument synthesis also records whitewashed-mudbrick completion for the mortuary and valley temples.
value_text: whitewashed mudbrick completing unfinished stone cores
locator: lines 28-30; compare SRC-EGY-MENKAURE main monument description
uncertainty: The exact completion stage at a single year around 2500 BCE depends on chronology; show a newly functional but materially expedient complex.

subject: Menkaure subsidiary pyramids
claim: The eastern subsidiary G III-a was formed as a true pyramid and at least partly granite-cased, while G III-b and G III-c remained uncased stepped cores.
value_text: one true pyramid and two uncased step pyramids
uncertainty: Ownerships and exact surface appearance are less secure than the excavated structural distinction.

subject: Khafre causeway
claim: Khafre's causeway was a narrow covered corridor; excavated wall surfaces were undecorated and retained no paint traces.
value_text: narrow covered undecorated corridor
uncertainty: The lost roof height and lighting remain reconstructed; do not add unsupported bright relief decoration.

subject: Sphinx complex
claim: The Sphinx Temple and quarry preserve evidence of unfinished work, including incomplete intended granite casing, raw megalithic limestone fabric, and irregular quarry cutting.
value_text: unfinished Sphinx Temple and quarry fabric
uncertainty: The degree of remaining construction debris and precise enclosure clearance at approximately 2500 BCE are not fixed.

subject: Heit el-Ghurab
claim: A crown-built Fourth Dynasty settlement of more than seven hectares lay about 400 metres south of the Sphinx and supported construction of the Giza pyramid complexes.
value_text: low urban settlement south of Sphinx
uncertainty: At approximately 2500 BCE it may have been in its final active phase or early demobilization; the local guide polygon is schematic.

subject: Wall of the Crow
claim: The Fourth Dynasty Wall of the Crow formed the northwest edge of Heit el-Ghurab, about 200 metres long and 10 metres high and thick at the base, with masonry faces left undressed and a monumental gateway.
value_text: 200 m long unfinished masonry wall
uncertainty: Function is debated and the rendered alignment is only an approximate guide; do not show later collapse.

subject: Khufu Eastern Cemetery
claim: Published expedition plans place royal-family mastabas in an organized cemetery east of Khufu's pyramid alongside the queens' pyramids.
value_text: orderly low mastaba rows east of Khufu
locator: plan details and linked G 7000 monuments
uncertainty: The cemetery expanded over time; the approximately 2500 BCE view must remain sparser than the complete excavated plan.

subject: Khufu Western Cemetery
claim: Expedition plans document the orthogonal G 4000 mastaba field in the Western Cemetery beside Khufu's complex.
value_text: orderly low mastaba rows west of Khufu
uncertainty: The necropolis grew over generations; use only the early organized core and avoid the density of the later Old Kingdom field.

subject: Royal pyramid complexes
claim: Pyramid temples, causeways, and valley temples served royal funerals and later offering cults maintained by priests and attendants.
value_text: priests offerings and processional activity
locator: Royal Pyramid Complexes lesson functional discussion
uncertainty: The number and exact placement of people in a single panorama are illustrative; keep activity restrained.
